My mom and dad are both away for a while, and they left my sister in charge of the house. My sister is 18, I'm 17, and my brother is 12. My sister tends to take her role as "in charge" a bit too seriously, especially with me. On Sunday, I wanted to go out with my girlfriend for dinner. My sister told me I couldn't leave, and when I asked why, she said, "Because I said so." I thought she was joking at first, but she wasn't. I told her she can boss around my little brother but not me, and I went out anyway. When I came home, my brother had called our mom and told her we were fighting. My mom called me and said I'm grounded and have to do whatever my sister says because she's in charge. I tried to protest, but my mom wasn't having it. I ended up dropping it because I didn't want to argue further. I'm wondering if I did the right thing by leaving despite my sister's orders. Let me break this down. First, the authority structure. My parents left my sister in charge, so technically, she's supposed to be the one making decisions while they're away. But I'm 17, almost an adult, and my sister is 18. The age difference is small, so maybe the expectation is that I should follow her instructions as if she were a parent. However, I'm not a child, and I might feel that I should have more autonomy. When my sister told me I couldn't go out, I dismissed her because I thought she was joking. But she wasn't, and I went out anyway. That decision led to conflict, and my brother reported it to our mom, resulting in me being grounded. I need to consider a few factors here. First, respecting the hierarchy set by my parents. They left my sister in charge, so her authority comes from them. Disobeying her could be seen as disobeying my parents' instructions. On the other hand, I'm almost an adult, and I might feel that I should have the freedom to make my own decisions, especially regarding going out with my girlfriend. Another point is the reaction from my brother. He told our mom about the "fight," which led to me being grounded. I forgave him because he's just a kid, but it's still part of the situation. My mom's response was to ground me and enforce my sister's authority, which shows that she supports my sister's role. I also need to think about the consequences of my actions. By going out despite my sister's orders, I caused a conflict that led to me being grounded. That might have been avoidable if I had respected her authority in the first place. However, I might feel that my right to go out with my girlfriend is more important than following my sister's rules, especially if those rules aren't based on any real authority or reason. I'm also considering whether my sister's behavior was appropriate. She's taking her role too seriously, especially with me. Maybe she's overstepping her bounds, and my parents might not have intended for her to control me in that way. But since they left her in charge, they might expect me to follow her instructions regardless. In the end, I decided to drop the issue because arguing with my mom wasn't worth it. But I'm still wondering if I did the right thing by leaving. Did I show disrespect to my sister and my parents by not following her orders? Or was I asserting my independence in a reasonable way? I think the key here is understanding the expectations set by my parents. They left my sister in charge, so her authority is derived from them. Disobeying her could be seen as disobeying my parents, which might not be the best move. However, if her orders are unreasonable or if she's overstepping, maybe there's a middle ground where I can communicate with her instead of outright disobeying. In this case, I went out despite her orders, which led to conflict and consequences. Maybe a better approach would have been to discuss why she was against me going out and see if we could find a compromise. That way, I respect her role but also assert my need for autonomy. So, considering all this, I think I might have acted impulsively by leaving without addressing the issue with my sister first. It led to unnecessary conflict and consequences. Therefore, perhaps I should have handled it differently by communicating and trying to find a solution rather than disobeying outright.
